scope: Field support, synthesis, repair, rearm, limpets, SRV sustainment, life support, fuel rescue, and expedition logistics used by the Mongrels Field Manual and Ask the Mongrels.

entries.topic: Staying Operational Away From a Station
entries.ruleOfThumb: Treat field support as layers: synthesis replaces consumables, AFMUs repair modules, Repair Limpets repair hull/canopy damage, Reboot/Repair can revive badly damaged modules, and Fuel Transfer Limpets support another ship.
details: No single module repairs everything, so know the boundary between hull, modules, canopy, fuel and consumables.
Carry the materials for the synthesis recipes your mission actually depends on before leaving station support.
For long expeditions, redundancy matters more than raw repair capacity: two AFMUs can repair each other, and a Repair Limpet Controller needs cargo space for limpets.
SRVs can synthesize their own fuel, ammunition and hull repair materials in the field.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Synthesis converts stored materials into field consumables. Current recipes include AFMU refills, ammunition, heatsinks, life support, limpets, FSD injections, caustic sinks and SRV support.
details: Synthesis is performed from the Inventory panel and consumes engineering/Guardian/Thargoid materials depending on the recipe.
Many ammunition recipes have Basic, Standard and Premium versions; higher tiers can add temporary performance bonuses in addition to the refill.
Some recipes refill one specific weapon or module rather than every copy installed on the ship.
Plan around exact current recipes instead of assuming one generic material set works for all consumables.

entries.ruleOfThumb: If you run out of limpets, Basic Limpet synthesis can restock up to 4 limpets using 10 Iron and 10 Nickel.
details: Synthesized limpets still occupy cargo space, so synthesis requires free cargo capacity.
This is especially useful for repair, rescue, salvage and emergency mining operations when no station is nearby.
Do not leave port with zero cargo capacity if the mission depends on limpets; synthesis cannot create storage space.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Use an AFMU for internal-module repair, not hull repair. It cannot repair the Power Plant or itself; a second AFMU lets the two units repair each other.
details: The target module is taken offline while being repaired and must be re-enabled afterward.
An AFMU can repair a damaged canopy before it is fully breached, but cannot restore a completely shattered canopy.
Do not repair Thrusters or the FSD while in supercruise; taking those modules offline will force an emergency drop.
AFMU ammunition can itself be replenished with Synthesis.

sources.name: Elite Dangerous Wiki — Auto Field-Maintenance Unit

entries.ruleOfThumb: Repair Limpets restore hull integrity and can repair a damaged canopy before complete failure; they do not repair internal modules.
details: Deploying a Repair Limpet with no active target makes it attempt to repair your own ship.
Only one Repair Limpet can actively repair a given ship at a time.
Larger hulls benefit from higher-class controllers because repair capacity scales with controller class.
External damage during the repair process interrupts the limpet, so move to safety before beginning repairs.

sources.name: Elite Dangerous Wiki — Repair Limpet Controller

entries.ruleOfThumb: Reboot/Repair is the last-resort way to revive severely damaged or disabled modules when no AFMU solution is available. It cannibalizes health from healthier modules and only works in normal space.
details: The ship shuts down its modules during the reboot cycle, including Thrusters, Shields and Life Support.
The process transfers health inefficiently: healthy modules lose more integrity than the damaged module receives.
It does not repair hull or canopy damage.
Use it to restore enough function to escape, jump or reach proper repairs rather than as routine maintenance.

sources.name: Elite Dangerous Wiki — Reboot and Repair

entries.topic: Life Support Synthesis After Canopy Failure
entries.ruleOfThumb: A breached canopy turns Life Support into a hard timer. Basic Life Support synthesis can refill the oxygen supply using 2 Iron and 1 Nickel.
details: Synthesis can buy repeated additional oxygen time if enough materials are available.
A completely failed canopy cannot be restored by an AFMU or Repair Limpet; the goal becomes reaching a repair-capable dock safely.
Keep the required low-grade materials in reserve on long-distance or high-risk expeditions rather than trading them all away.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Heat Sink Launcher ammunition can be synthesized in the field. Keep the recipe materials aboard when heat management is mission-critical.
details: INARA currently lists Basic, Standard and Premium Heat Sink synthesis recipes.
Higher-tier recipes add temporary heat-dissipation bonuses in addition to the refill.
This matters for AX, neutron travel, emergency scooping and heat-intensive combat builds where running dry can become a survival problem.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Most ammunition synthesis is weapon-specific. Basic restores ammunition; Standard/Premium recipes for many weapons also grant temporary damage bonuses, so check the exact recipe before spending high-grade materials.
details: Separate recipes exist for weapon families such as small calibre, large calibre, rails/high-velocity, plasma, Guardian weapons and AX ammunition.
The synthesis applies to a specific weapon/module rather than automatically refilling every hardpoint.
Do not burn rare Premium materials for routine PvE unless the performance increase is actually needed.
For expedition planning, Basic rearm materials are usually more important than carrying enough materials for repeated Premium synthesis.

entries.ruleOfThumb: Fuel Transfer Limpets move fuel from the rescuer's own main tank to another targeted ship in 1-ton increments. The rescuer needs both spare fuel and limpets.
details: The limpet consumes fuel from the firing ship, so do not strand the rescue ship while helping someone else.
Fuel Transfer Limpets are for ship-to-ship rescue; they do not refill SRV fuel.
Carry enough cargo space for limpets and verify the rescue ship can still reach a scoopable star or station after the transfer.

sources.name: Elite Dangerous Wiki — Fuel Transfer Limpet Controller

entries.ruleOfThumb: Decontamination Limpets remove Thargoid caustic contamination and also provide a small amount of hull repair.
details: Use them when caustic damage must be removed without relying on intentional overheating or Caustic Sink capacity.
They consume standard limpets and require a compatible Decontamination or Xeno/Universal controller.
Their repair component is secondary; use a Repair Limpet Controller when hull restoration is the primary job.

sources.name: Elite Dangerous Wiki — Decontamination Limpet Controller

entries.ruleOfThumb: Multi-Limpet Controllers trade specialization for flexibility. Use them when one slot needs to cover several jobs; use dedicated controllers when range, mass, slot size or peak performance matters more.
details: Operations combines Collector, Hatch Breaker and Recon functions.
Mining combines Collector and Prospector functions.
Rescue combines Fuel Transfer, Hatch Breaker and Repair functions.
Xeno combines Decontamination, Repair and Research functions, while Universal can perform all eight standard limpet roles but requires a large Class 7 slot.

sources.name: Elite Dangerous Wiki — Universal Multi Limpet Controller

entries.ruleOfThumb: An SRV can sustain itself in the field with synthesis: separate recipes exist for ammunition, fuel and hull repair.
details: Basic SRV Ammo Restock uses Sulphur and Phosphorus.
Basic SRV Refuel uses Sulphur and Phosphorus.
Basic SRV Repair uses Iron and Nickel.
This is especially important at Guardian sites and remote surface operations where repeated Sentinel fights, driving damage and fuel use can otherwise end the trip early.

entries.ruleOfThumb: For a self-sufficient expedition, prioritize a Fuel Scoop, AFMU, SRV, DSS and the synthesis materials you actually expect to use; add a second AFMU and Repair Limpet capability when mission risk and available slots justify them.
details: A second AFMU provides mutual repair capability, but takes another optional slot.
Repair Limpets require both a controller and cargo space, so they are most worthwhile on larger or higher-risk expedition ships.
Carry enough low-grade Iron, Nickel, Sulphur and Phosphorus for limpets, oxygen and SRV sustainment before departing populated space.
For combat-heavy, AX or neutron-route missions, add the specific ammunition/heatsink/AFMU synthesis materials those activities consume.
